name: Tayla Holman
headline: Freelance healthcare communications writer, editor & content strategist
specialties: translating clinical complexity into plain, accessible language
writing for both lay/patient and executive/clinical (HCP) audiences
proof_points: 61 pieces across 7 verticals for GE HealthCare
116 articles across 6 regional networks for HCA Healthcare
education: M.S. in Health Communication, Boston University
B.A. in Print Journalism & English, Hofstra University
voice_notes: Warm, sincere, and confident without being deferential — never gushing, salesy, or over-eager. Opens with a specific, researched hook (a real observation about the company or its work) on cold outreach, or a direct reference to what the other person said on a warm reply — never generic throat-clearing like 'I'm reaching out because.' Leads with genuine interest or connection before credentials, then backs claims with specifics — named pieces, real clients, concrete experience — rather than adjectives or self-praise. Demonstrates fit by proposing actual content ideas and by choosing work samples that show range across registers (patient/lay to executive/HCP, B2C to B2B). States rates and logistics plainly and without apology. Flexes length to context: longer and case-building for a cold pitch to an admired organization; tighter and more business-forward for a warm reply or an inbound. Closes low-pressure, offering a call, with no false urgency. Underlying content voice is clear, credible, and accessible — translates clinical complexity into plain language without losing accuracy.
